solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: H.H. Munro comes round March 2nd and 3rd for 10 Oramo

indicators.note: the writer's pen name wraps itself around the two picked letters, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: H.H. Munro wrote short stories under the pen name Saki
the second and third letters of the word March are A and R

explanation.surface: An Edwardian short-story writer seems to be turning up in early March, oddly cross-referenced to a Finnish conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: In this themed puzzle '10' stands for the answer to 10 Across, a conductor, so '10 Oramo' asks for the first name of the conductor surnamed Oramo.
explanation.definitionFit: Sakari Oramo is a Finnish conductor, so his first name completes the phrase conductor ___ Oramo.

clue.text: Stunning 10-0 triumph first for 10

indicators.note: a stunning blow knocks things about, so the assembled letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: 10 points to the answer of 10 Across, a word for a great conductor
the figure zero, in a football score, is nil

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word triumph is taken on its own

explanation.surface: A sports report of a stunning ten-nil victory.
explanation.walkthrough: '10-0' looks like a scoreline but is two pieces: the 10 Across word and NIL for zero. With T from 'triumph first' they are rearranged as signalled by 'Stunning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Simon Rattle is a celebrated British conductor, long associated with Birmingham and Berlin.

clue.text: 10 Otto at Kuala Lumpur with sovereign ruler, reportedly

parts.note: KL is the usual abbreviation for Kuala Lumpur, capital of Malaysia

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the ruler's title is taken for how it is spoken

parts.note: an emperor is a sovereign ruler of an empire

explanation.surface: A conductor visits the Malaysian capital in the company of a monarch, so the gossip goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The last three letters are spelt as the unstressed ending of the ruler's title sounds, ER rather than OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto Klemperer was a German-born conductor famous for his Beethoven and Mahler.

clue.text: See 1
10 could admit "Am Ernest"

indicators.note: the conductor could own up to these words, and what he admits to is a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A conductor might well confess that his first name is Ernest.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the conductor really was called Ernest, so the anagram of his own words gives his surname; 'admit' only frames the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Ansermet was a Swiss conductor who founded the Orchestre de la Suisse Romande.

clue.text: Square in Clacton in Essex

indicators.note: the first in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is asking about a town square in the seaside resort of Clacton, Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Clacton-on-Sea is a seaside town in the English county of Essex. 'Square' is not a plaza but a number that is another number multiplied by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Three times three makes this number, so it is a perfect square in arithmetic.

clue.text: Solver said record is English hymn

indicators.note: said tells us the word for the solver is taken by its sound only

parts.note: the person solving the clue is addressed as you
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone claims the solver made a recording of an English hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hymn' is a verb here, meaning to sing the praises of.
explanation.definitionFit: To hymn someone is to praise them highly, which is what a formal tribute speech does.

clue.text: A weaver raised dough

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters are lifted to read from bottom to top

parts.note: a loom is the machine that weaves cloth

explanation.surface: A weaver, perhaps a baker on the side, gets the dough to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' is slang for money, not bread mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for cash, so the definition is a straight synonym.

clue.text: 10 Arturo at opera, mounting popular new one

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means the word goes upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A conductor at the opera house is putting on a popular new production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' looks like staging a production but turns IN upwards to NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was the Italian conductor who led La Scala and the NBC Symphony Orchestra.

clue.text: Legendary horned creature roaming moors once

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A mythical horned beast once wandered the moors.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for the unicorn, the one-horned beast of legend, and also a constellation.

clue.text: 1980s Austin model having some art form

indicators.note: form as a verb means to shape, so the letters are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A 1980s British car is said to have some artistic shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art form' reads as one phrase, but 'form' is the anagram signal working on 'some art'.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin Rover sold a family hatchback under this name from 1983, the car the clue's model refers to.

clue.text: Sailor's holds for 10 Andris

definitions.meaning: belonging to the famous admiral, Horatio Nelson, Britain's best-known sailor
full and half ... are wrestling holds with the arms locked behind an opponent's neck
Andris ... is a Latvian conductor, music director in Boston and Leipzig

explanation.surface: A sailor's wrestling grips are linked to a conductor named Andris.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling holds share the admiral's surname, and the Latvian conductor's surname is the same word.

clue.text: Card game. Solo, maybe

definitions.meaning: a trick-taking card game, often shortened to nap
... Solo was the spy hero of The Man from U.N.C.L.E., so Solo is his surname

explanation.surface: Someone names a card game and suggests solo whist as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Solo is itself a card game, which pulls toward a single definition; it is in fact a surname whose first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The trick-taking game nap takes its full name from the French emperor, as does the TV spy Mr Solo.

clue.text: Reptile of Antiguan antiquity

indicators.note: of here means drawn out of the following words, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A lizard dating from Antigua's distant past.
explanation.definitionFit: This large tropical American lizard is a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Comic effect of puppet, holding redhead's head

indicators.note: the puppet word holds a letter within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a doll can be a puppet or figure
read as the head of red, its first letter R
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A puppet show gets a laugh with a red-haired figure's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead's head' is split: 'redhead's' gives the head of red, R, and 'head' alone is NESS, a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being droll means being amusingly odd, so the quality of drollery is a comic effect.

clue.text: 10 Bohm knew all Rossini's libretti, for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so each of the four words gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A conductor is credited with knowing every one of Rossini's opera texts.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Böhm was an Austrian conductor renowned for Mozart and Strauss.

clue.text: He decreed a dome but would baulk over eastern inn

indicators.note: over can mean upset or knocked over, so the letters of baulk are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: a khan is a caravanserai, an inn for travellers in the East

explanation.surface: A ruler ordered a dome built but might shy away from staying at an inn in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes Coleridge's poem: 'In Xanadu did Kubla Khan / A stately pleasure-dome decree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's poem has the Mongol emperor decree a stately pleasure-dome, so this is a literary allusion.

clue.text: 10 upset geologist, king admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the king's letter goes inside the rearranged letters
upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A conductor has upset a geologist after a king was let in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Georg Solti was a Hungarian-born conductor famed for the first studio recording of Wagner's Ring.

clue.text: Racket as girl embraces injured don

indicators.note: the girl's name embraces, holding the other letters within it

parts.note: Louise is a girl's name

indicators.note: injured means damaged or knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A row breaks out as a girl hugs a hurt academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' is a din, not a tennis bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a din, which is exactly an uproarious, clamorous sound.

clue.text: Two sentences for the avian community

parts.note: bird, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time, is British slang for a jail sentence
a life sentence is the prison term that runs for the rest of one's days, the second of the two terms

explanation.surface: Two prison terms are handed down to the bird world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two sentences' supplies both halves from the one word. 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving time in prison (rhyming slang: bird-lime, time).
explanation.definitionFit: Feathered creatures of an area taken together form its avian population.

clue.text: Hallé 10's cutting remark to team about drum beat

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the team's letters sit around the drum beat

parts.note: a team such as a football or cricket side has eleven players, written 11 and read as II
a roll is a rapid drum beat

explanation.surface: A conductor makes a sharp comment to the band about the drumming.
explanation.walkthrough: The team is eleven, 11, read as two letter Is. The Hallé is a Manchester orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Barbirolli was the long-serving principal conductor of Manchester's Hallé Orchestra.

clue.text: 10 Riccardo is a crew member on The Bounty. Not half, he is!

indicators.note: not half of means only half is kept, here the front half of the eight-letter word

parts.words: a crew member on The Bounty
parts.note: the Bounty's crew famously mutinied against Captain Bligh

explanation.surface: A conductor is cast as one of the Bounty rebels, and the exclamation insists he really is one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half, he is!' plays on the British exclamation 'not half!' meaning 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Riccardo Muti is an Italian conductor, long at La Scala and the Chicago Symphony.

clue.text: See 25
10 Claudio at pop-group's party

parts.note: Abba is the Swedish pop group
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A conductor turns up at a party thrown by a pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Abbado was an Italian conductor who led La Scala, Vienna and the Berlin Philharmonic.

clue.text: Save about one pound and made a house

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the other letters

parts.note: save as a preposition means except, which is but
the Roman numeral for one is I
L stands for libra, the pound

explanation.surface: Someone saved about a pound and managed to put up a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb about money but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Constructing a dwelling is to have put one up, the past tense of the construction verb.

clue.text: Sleepers, awake! is no cure for this!

definitions.text: Sleepers, awake! is no cure for this!

parts.words: Sleepers, awake! is no cure for this!
parts.note: Sleepers, Awake is a Bach cantata; telling people to wake up does nothing for someone who cannot fall asleep

explanation.surface: A wry remark that Bach's cantata Sleepers, Awake! will not help a sufferer.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition is an inability to sleep, so a call to wake up hardly cures it.

clue.text: 10 revised atonal triad

indicators.note: revised means altered or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor has rewritten an atonal three-note chord.
explanation.definitionFit: Antal Doráti was a Hungarian-born conductor known for recording all of Haydn's symphonies.

clue.text: Channel broadcasting cricket to eastern isle

parts.note: Sky Sports holds the TV rights to English cricket

explanation.surface: A TV channel showing cricket to an island in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is the British satellite TV company whose sports channels show live cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: 10 Bernard on part of Hispaniola with new knight

parts.note: Haiti occupies the western part of the Caribbean island of Hispaniola
K is the abbreviation for knight, as in KBE

explanation.surface: A conductor finds himself in the Caribbean with a newly made knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard Haitink was a Dutch conductor, long chief of Amsterdam's Concertgebouw Orchestra.

clue.text: Like Britain — is Great, maybe

indicators.note: maybe means possibly, signalling the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Britain is described as Great, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the island's own name, Great Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is an island ringed by water, which is what the poetic compound means.

clue.text: Last of women treated badly — were gossips

indicators.note: the final letter of the word women is taken
badly means in a damaged way, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Women complain of being treated badly while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Chattering idly, as gossips do, means chatting on at length.

clue.text: Direct telephone connection with Alabama

parts.note: a phone line is a telephone connection
AL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: A direct phone link to Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' looks like part of 'direct line' but is the definition, in the sense of direct descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent in a straight line from parent to child is direct descent, an adjective of ancestry.
